items.title: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough
items.description: It was the latest wave in a displacement crisis that has been building in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region for a decade, and there is no sign it is reversing. items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. items.title: SJS mourns Somali radio journalist Hassan Kafi Qoyste who died at 57
items.description: Ayanle Hassan, Qoyste's son, told SJS that his father, who was diabetic, fell ill on Friday night and was rushed to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The late Qoyste was a veteran journalist and one of the most remarkable radio journalists in Somalia, known for his distinctive and memorable voice. He first worked as an archive manager at the Ministry of Labour of the Somali central government in the 1980s before joining the print media in Mogadishu in the early 1990s, as the country descended into civil war. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud

items.title: Somali Journalist Mohamed Aweys Moodey Dies After Stabbing in Germany
items.description: The incident reportedly occurred at a residential facility. German authorities have identified a 28-year-old Somali man as the suspect. Police and prosecutors are investigating the circumstances of the incident, including the motive and whether it was connected to an earlier dispute between the two men. Moodey was a veteran journalist who worked in Somali media for many years. In 2014, he was arrested in Ethiopia and later sentenced to 27 years in prison under the country's anti-terrorism laws.
